title: Wire Private observability minimum pack into redwood-helm-charts (dashboards, alerts, log pipeline) with versioned values
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Goal
Wire the Private Observability Minimum Pack artifacts into `redwood-helm-charts` so Private installs get a supported, turnkey baseline for metrics/alerts/dashboards/log collection with sane defaults and explicit versioning.

This ticket is NOT about authoring the dashboards/alerts themselves; it’s about packaging + install surfaces + default values + upgrade safety.

Scope
1) Grafana dashboards
- Ship the minimum-pack dashboards as packaged artifacts (ConfigMaps or sidecar-mounted) with deterministic names and folder placement.
- Create a consistent dashboard taxonomy/folder: "Redwood / Private" and subfolders (Runtime, Control Plane, Infra).
- Ensure dashboards render with bounded label cardinality (align with ENG-19143) and do not require internet access.

2) Prometheus rules
- Wire in minimum-pack recording rules + alert rules into the chart (PrometheusRule CRs if kube-prometheus-stack is present; otherwise plain rule files + documented integration).
- Add enable/disable toggles for: recording rules, alerts, and any optional exporters.
- Ensure alert annotations include runbook links (oncall feedback) and the default severity taxonomy (ticket vs page).

3) Log pipeline defaults
- Provide a default log collector deployment (or chart integration) suitable for Private: structured log parsing, batching/backpressure defaults, safe redaction guidance.
- Expose supported sinks via values (Loki, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Splunk HEC, OTLP as optional), but keep the default sink minimal and safe.
- Default retention guidance is documentation-level; avoid hardcoding storage retention outside Prometheus/Grafana PVC sizing defaults.

4) Versioning + upgrade safety
- Add an explicit `observabilityPack.version` value that pins the bundled artifacts (dashboards + rules + collector config).
- Make upgrading safe: if dashboard IDs/UIDs change, we must avoid blank dashboards after upgrade.
- Provide migration notes for any required manual steps (ideally none for v1).

5) Private installer integration surface
- Ensure values are compatible with `redwood-private-installer` (PRs tracked separately), including offline/airgap packaging.
- Provide a small post-install verification section in chart notes/README (scrapes present, dashboards loaded, alerts visible but not paging by default).

Out of scope
- Premium observability (long retention, federation, advanced tracing sampling).
- Customer-specific dashboard customization beyond values overrides.

Primary stakeholders
- Diego Santos (assignee): helm wiring + private install integration
- Dylan Brooks: dashboards/tooling integration feedback
- Sergio Costa: rules/dashboards authoring alignment
- Rafael Mendes / Neha Kapoor: SRE validation + default alert posture
- Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei: security review for logging defaults + redaction

Implementation plan (proposed)
A) Chart structure
- Create `charts/redwood-private-observability` (or `charts/observability-pack`) that can be enabled from the main private umbrella chart.
- Support two modes:
  1. "Bring your own" Prometheus/Grafana: only ship ConfigMaps/PrometheusRule resources, no operator installation.
  2. "Reference stack" (optional): install a lightweight Prometheus+Grafana if customer opts in (default OFF for Private).

B) Values
- Add a single top-level block under private chart values:
  - `observability.enabled` (default true for Private)
  - `observability.packVersion` (default pinned)
  - `observability.dashboards.enabled` (default true)
  - `observability.alerts.enabled` (default true but paging-class alerts disabled by default)
  - `observability.recordingRules.enabled` (default true)
  - `observability.logs.enabled` (default true)
  - `observability.logs.sink` (default "none" or "loki" depending on install profile; see Decisions)
  - `observability.resources.*` (CPU/mem requests/limits)

C) Defaults philosophy
- Defaults must be safe for typical customer clusters and bounded in cost:
  - Do not page by default unless the customer explicitly enables paging (or wires to their pager).
  - Avoid high-cardinality dashboards that melt Prometheus.
  - Log collector must not drop logs silently; if buffers fill, surface metrics/alerts for backpressure.

Acceptance criteria
- `helm template` produces:
  - Dashboard ConfigMaps (or equivalent) with deterministic labels/annotations for sidecar pickup.
  - Prometheus rules resources with runbook links in annotations.
  - Log collector manifests with sane resource requests and configurable sinks.
- In a reference Private cluster (staging):
  - Grafana shows "Redwood / Private" dashboards populated within 10 minutes of install.
  - Prometheus shows targets UP for Redwood components and rules loaded (no parse errors).
  - Alerts exist and are in a non-paging default posture (ticket-only severities enabled; paging-class disabled unless explicitly enabled).
  - Log pipeline sends Redwood control plane + runtime logs to the configured sink and redacts obvious secrets.
- Offline/airgap compatibility:
  - All artifacts are packaged such that an air-gapped install does not fetch dashboards/rules from the internet.

Links
- GitHub PR (expected): `sources/github/redwood-helm-charts/pr-18405-wire-observability-pack-into-private-values.json`
- Dashboard bundle PR: `sources/github/observability-pack/pr-18341-add-private-minimum-pack-dashboard-bundle.json`
- Alert rules PRs: `sources/github/observability-pack/pr-18356-add-private-prometheus-alert-rules-latency-and-availability.json`, `sources/github/observability-pack/pr-18372-add-gpu-saturation-and-oom-alerts.json`
- Installer preflight/postinstall validation: `sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr-18422-add-observability-preflight-and-postinstall-validation.json`

Risks / open questions
- Grafana dashboard UID collisions across upgrades: ensure stable UIDs; avoid regeneration.
- Customer clusters without kube-prometheus-stack: need a documented and tested integration path (PrometheusRule CRDs won’t exist).
- Default log sink: choose a posture that doesn’t force customers into Loki if they already have ELK/Splunk.
- NetworkPolicies: scrapes can break when customers lock down namespaces; installer preflight should warn, but chart should also expose explicit ports/labels to allowlist.

Decisions (tentative)
- Default to shipping artifacts (dashboards + rules + collector) but do not install Prometheus/Grafana by default.
- Default alerting: enable recording rules + non-paging alerts; paging-class alerts behind `observability.alerts.pagingEnabled=false`.
- Log collector default sink = "none" (collector runs and writes to stdout only) unless a sink is configured; document recommended sinks per environment.

Definition of done
- Chart PR merged, pinned pack version documented, and validated in private staging + smoke tests green.
- Release notes snippet provided to Docs/PM.

2025-07-25 (Diego Santos): Initial implementation plan: add `observability` block under private values and ship dashboards as ConfigMaps with grafana-sidecar labels. Need confirmation from Dylan/Chloe on folder + naming conventions.
2025-07-29 (Dylan Brooks): Prefer folder "Redwood / Private" with subfolders Runtime, Control Plane, Infra. Please keep dashboard UIDs stable; we’ve been burned by blank dashboards after upgrades.
2025-08-01 (Rafael Mendes): SRE request: paging-class alerts OFF by default. Ticket-only alerts OK but include runbook links + clear first-action steps in annotations.

2025-08-05 (Marcus Lin): Security note: log collector must not forward request/response bodies by default. Ensure redaction for auth headers and any accidental tokens. Add explicit warning text in values for enabling payload logging (if ever).

2025-08-08 (Diego Santos): Implemented PrometheusRule resources behind `observability.prometheusRules.enabled`. If CRD missing, manifests won’t apply; adding a NOTES.txt warning + docs link. Still need a better path for non-operator Prometheus (rule file export).
2025-08-12 (Sergio Costa): Alert annotations updated to include runbook placeholders. Please wire `runbookBaseUrl` value so Private installs can point to customer-internal URLs if needed.

2025-08-15 (Diego Santos): Opened PR wiring pack into helm charts; includes `packVersion` pin + checksum annotations on ConfigMaps to force rollout on change. Request review from SRE + Security on defaults.

2025-08-19 (Allison Grant): Please ensure label cardinality is bounded in dashboards (avoid `tenant_id` and full `route` label). For Private minimum pack, aggregate by service/namespace/pod and optionally by model family only.
